warnings: EVERY BEAM MARK USED ON S-01 AND S-02 IS DETAILED HERE, CHECKED BOTH WAYS. The plans use B1, B1A, B2, B2A, B2B, B2C, B2D, B3, B3A, B3B, B3C, B4, B4A - thirteen marks - and this sheet details exactly those thirteen, with no mark detailed that the plans never use. No dangling callout in either direction.

FOUR MARKS HAVE A CURTAILED BAR ROW AND ITS FACE WAS DECIDED FROM THE LEADER, NOT THE LABEL TEXT - this is the §7 trap and it was worked mark by mark, not by reusing one answer. B2 (2-ø12 หยุดที่ L/8), B2B (2-ø12 หยุดที่ L/8), B2C (2-ø12, no L/8 text) and B3A (3-ø20 หยุดที่ L/8) each print an extra row between the top and bottom labels. On all four the leader lands at about 70-75% of the section depth - well below mid-depth and immediately above the bottom cluster, about 0.07-0.08 m clear of it - so all four merge into main_bar.bottom as a second bottom layer, with the printed text preserved in the face's note. None is recorded as main_bar.middle: §6 reserves that for a row sitting BETWEEN the clusters at mid-depth, and none of these does. None is left in additional_bars either, per §7's rule that a curtailed bar still belongs to the face it sits on.

B2B AND B2C MIX DIAMETERS IN THE BOTTOM FACE (2-ø16 full length plus 2-ø12 curtailed). Recorded per §0.5 with dia_mm = 16 (the first/dominant), mixed_dia_mm = [16, 12] and the full printed text in dia_mm_printed_as, so the split is recoverable.

B3B IS A VARIABLE-DEPTH BEAM, printed 0.40~0.50. It is the sloping balcony-roof beam. height_mm records the shallow end (400) and the full printed range is kept in height_mm_printed_as; a consumer needing the deep end must read the printed value, not the number.

2C-2C DOES NOT PRINT ITS OWN DEPTH. The section gives only the 0.15 width. The 400 mm depth is taken from the B2A/B2C longitudinal elevation printed immediately to its left on the same sheet, which dimensions 0.40 along the whole run. Flagged on the element rather than left blank, because the elevation is unambiguous and on the same sheet.

B4 AND B4A ARE UPPER-FLOOR-ONLY MARKS. They appear on S-02 and nowhere on S-01. They are the only 0.50 m deep beams in the house and the only ones with variable stirrup spacing (@0.125 at the ends, @0.20 mid-span); spacing_mm records the smallest per §0.5 with variable_spacing: true and the detail in the note.

Ø IS RECORDED AS type RB EVERYWHERE ON THIS SHEET, per §6 - every bar is drawn with the Ø symbol and none with ribs. The S-01 note that ø12 มม. ขึ้นไปใช้ SD-30 is a project-level material grade recorded on S-01's own file; it is deliberately not used to override the printed symbol here, because §6 says never infer the type from the diameter.
ป- IS THE THAI ABBREVIATION FOR ปลอก (stirrup) AND IS ALWAYS RECORDED AS stirrup, never tie/tie_bar (§0.6). It appears on all thirteen marks.

THREE LONGITUDINAL ELEVATIONS CARRY SPAN AND CURTAILMENT DIMENSIONS the cross-sections do not: B2A/B2C (0.90 + 0.20 + 0.90 top-bar extensions, runs marked vary and 3.50, 0.36), B3/B3C/B3B (1.00 + 0.20 + 1.00 and 0.90 + 0.10 + 0.75, runs vary / 0.40 / 4.00 / 0.46 / vary), B4/B4A (1.30 + 0.20 + 1.30 and 1.35, runs 3.50 and 5.20 with 0.50 and 0.65 overhangs). The span_length_m recorded on B4 and B4A comes from those elevations; the other marks' spans vary per location and are recorded per occurrence on the plan files instead, so no single span is claimed for them here.
The word vary is printed on the B2A and B3 elevations where the run length differs by location - recorded as printed, not resolved to a number.
